sermon.title: Miracles and Healings
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer surveys the Bible’s miracles, then shows the key to healing: people came to hear the word, to be healed, and were healed by Jesus whose presence was there to heal. God grants signs as he wills, praise brings his presence, the song service is equal to preaching, and love—not faith—raised Lazarus and the widow’s son.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Rough captions; many fixes and several phrases not clear. He names Elijah as the prophet in 2 Kings 3 (it was Elisha). Points to check: angels without wings (seraphim and cherubim are described with wings); dead raised “six times” in the New Testament; reports from the late-1940s healing movement (an Illinois doctor, a leg tumor). Sensitive content kept as spoken: water baptism essential for salvation, prayer-cloth ministries, races made at Babel, U.S. foreign policy (“we created that mess” in the Middle East). Congregation musicians are named in passing in the transcript.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

faqs.question: Was creation in six days?
faqs.answer: He says yes—God spoke and it happened, not over millions of years.

faqs.question: Do angels have wings?
faqs.answer: He says angels do not have wings, contrary to Christmas pictures.

faqs.question: Did the wise men visit the manger?
faqs.answer: No—he says they went into a house.

faqs.question: Why did multitudes come to Jesus?
faqs.answer: To hear the word and to be healed.

faqs.question: What is the greatest miracle?
faqs.answer: Salvation—turning a person from sin to righteousness and from damnation to eternal life.

faqs.question: What does it mean to praise?
faqs.answer: To brag and boast about God and give him honor.

faqs.question: Is water baptism necessary?
faqs.answer: He says water baptism is essential for salvation, as Paul and Silas baptized the jailer the same night.

faqs.question: Do new believers need many words to worship?
faqs.answer: No—it isn’t how many words but how genuine; he could only say “I love Jesus” as a young Christian.

faqs.question: Is someone not healed a second-class Christian?
faqs.answer: No—God does what he wants, when and how he wants.
